While it is on, QA Wrap keeps the last 2 minutes of your clicks and typing, the console and the network calls (address, status and time only, no bodies) in the memory of that page. popup.partitions.bb.why.badColor: A colour input only holds #rrggbb. A scripted post can send anything.
popup.partitions.bb.why.beforeMin: One invalid class before the minimum.
popup.partitions.bb.why.belowBoth: Everything under the minimum behaves the same way, so one value covers it.
popup.partitions.bb.why.belowOne: One invalid class below the bound.
popup.partitions.bb.why.decimal: Valid only if the step allows it. A quantity that accepts 1.5 is a defect you can only find deliberately.
popup.partitions.bb.why.emptyOptional: The field is optional, so absent is a valid state and must be tested as one.
popup.partitions.bb.why.emptyRequired: The field is required, so nothing is an invalid class of its own.
popup.partitions.bb.why.fileAccepted: The valid class the field declares.
popup.partitions.bb.why.fileNoneOptional: Optional, so it is a valid state.
popup.partitions.bb.why.fileNoneRequired: Required, so nothing attached is an invalid class.
popup.partitions.bb.why.fileOversized: The limit is on the server and is almost never stated in the page, so it is found by exceeding it.
popup.partitions.bb.why.fileWrong: The accept attribute filters the chooser and refuses nothing: a wrong type still arrives by drag and drop and by a scripted post.
popup.partitions.bb.why.impossibleDate: 29 February in a non-leap year. Its own class because it is well-formed and still wrong.
popup.partitions.bb.why.impossibleOrdere: A well-formed value that names nothing real (29 February in a non-leap year, a week that does not exist). Its own class because it is well-formed and still wrong.
popup.partitions.bb.why.impossibleTime: Well-formed in shape and still wrong: minutes and hours stop at 59 and 23. Its own class because a loose parser lets it through.
popup.partitions.bb.why.inverted: The minimum is higher than the maximum, so no value can be valid. This is a bug in the form.
popup.partitions.bb.why.needsPattern: The field declares pattern="{pattern}", so no sample is made up for it. Type a value that matches the pattern.
popup.partitions.bb.why.negative: Undeclared, and almost never intended for an amount or a count. Worth one test to find out which.
popup.partitions.bb.why.noAt: One invalid class: structurally not an address.
popup.partitions.bb.why.noDomain: A separate class. Some validators catch the missing @ and not this.
popup.partitions.bb.why.nonNumeric: The browser blocks it in the field; the server usually does not, and the server is what stores it.
popup.partitions.bb.why.noneOptional: Optional, so this is the state a fresh form starts in and has to be tested.
popup.partitions.bb.why.noneRequired: Required, so an unchosen control is an invalid class and submitting must be refused.
popup.partitions.bb.why.offList: The list is enforced in the page, not usually on the server. This is the class a scripted post finds and a mouse never can.
popup.partitions.bb.why.offStep: Between two steps of the grid. The browser flags it in the field; the server often stores it as it arrived.
popup.partitions.bb.why.option: One offered value. Offered values are one class each only where the application treats them differently; where it does not, one test covers several.
popup.partitions.bb.why.overnightGap: The gap of an overnight range: after the maximum and before the minimum.
popup.partitions.bb.why.patternFail: The field declares pattern="{pattern}", so anything outside it is a class of its own.
popup.partitions.bb.why.shorterThan: One invalid class below the length bound.
popup.partitions.bb.why.telLetters: A phone field expects digits. Letters are a class of their own, and a form with no format check lets them through.
popup.partitions.bb.why.telShort: Too few digits to be a phone number.
popup.partitions.bb.why.tooLongEmail: Well-formed, but over the declared maximum length.
popup.partitions.bb.why.tooLongMax: The browser truncates it in the field, which is exactly why it has to be sent another way as well: the server may not.
popup.partitions.bb.why.tooLongNoMax: No maximum is declared, so the real limit is the database column, and nobody declared that either.
popup.partitions.bb.why.unicodeEmail: type=email refuses a non-ASCII local part in the browser (RFC 6531 allows it, many systems still reject it). A class of its own; valid only where a pattern admits it.
popup.partitions.bb.why.untickedOptional: Optional, so unticked is a valid state and has to be tested as one rather than assumed.
popup.partitions.bb.why.untickedRequired: The field is required, so leaving it unticked is an invalid class and must be refused.
popup.partitions.bb.why.validOvernight: The valid class. The range runs overnight: min is after max, so it wraps past midnight.
popup.partitions.bb.why.validUnlessMax: Valid unless a maximum says otherwise.
popup.partitions.bb.why.validUnlessMin: Valid unless a minimum says otherwise.
popup.partitions.bb.why.whitespace: Distinct from empty: a naive "not empty" check lets it through and the record is saved blank.

tools.a11y.label: Check accessibility
tools.a11y.one: List what would stop somebody using this page with a screen reader or a keyboard.
tools.a11y.what: Runs the same engine that Chrome DevTools uses, and lists what would stop someone using a screen reader or a keyboard.
tools.a11y.why: Every rule it breaks is listed under "Findings" on this card, with the elements and a button that scrolls each one into view and rings it. The findings also go into the session, so they are in the report next to everything else, and the panel has a full rule list and 12 checks a machine cannot make.
tools.api.label: Send a request
tools.api.one: Call the site’s own API as the user who is logged in, without copying a token into another app.
tools.api.optionsLabel: What this is for, with an example
tools.api.what: Opens a page where you can write an API request by hand and send it from this browser, so the cookies the site has already set go with it. Method, URL, headers, body, environments with {{variables}}, and a short list of commands that run before it is sent. The endpoints this session already watched can be imported and re-sent with one header changed.
tools.api.why: Checking an endpoint mid-flow usually means copying a token into a separate app and losing the session. This keeps the session: the request is authenticated the way the page is, the answer is on screen with its status, its time and its headers, and both go into the timeline and the Postman export beside the traffic the application made on its own.
tools.autofill.label: Fill the form
tools.autofill.one: Fill every field at once with a value a tester would have chosen, and name what it could not.
tools.autofill.optionsLabel: What it fills, and what it could not
tools.autofill.what: Fills every field on the page with the value a tester would have chosen: a real-shaped phone number, an IBAN that passes its checksum, a date inside the allowed range, an amount between min and max, and in Arabic where the page is Arabic. It does not press submit.
tools.autofill.why: A random word in every box gets a form submitted; a designed value gets it tested. Every field it filled, every field the page rejected and every field it left alone is listed under "Result" on this card, so a partial run is legible instead of looking like a failure.
tools.blackbox.label: Design the values
tools.blackbox.one: Point at a field and get the handful of values worth testing, and why each one.
tools.blackbox.what: Press "Pick a field" and click any field on the page. This reads what the field itself declares (its type, its minimum, its maximum, its options, whether it is required) and works out the distinct classes of input it has, plus the exact values on each edge.
tools.blackbox.why: Trying forty random values covers less than four chosen ones. This tells you which four, and names each one so you can say what you tested rather than that you "tried some things". It reads dropdowns, radios, tickboxes, sliders, file choosers and rich-text editors as well as text boxes.
tools.break.label: Break a request
tools.break.one: Make the site fail on purpose, then stop it failing without reloading anything.
tools.break.what: Makes the site fail on purpose: a 500 error, a dead connection, a slow reply, or a request sent somewhere else entirely.
tools.break.why: Lets you see how the app behaves when the server misbehaves, without needing anyone to break the server. Rules stack. "Stop breaking it" takes every rule off at once: the next request goes through normally, nothing reloads, and everything the broken requests already put in the session stays there.
tools.diagram.label: Draw the flow
tools.diagram.one: Turn what you just did into a workflow diagram on one page.
tools.diagram.what: Turns what you did so far into a workflow diagram on one A4 page: start, each step, a decision where the application answered, a red box where it failed, the end, with the user story beside it in Arabic.
tools.diagram.why: A picture of the flow is what a product owner asks for and a tester never has time to draw. Every box and arrow can be moved, reworded and recoloured; the legend explains itself.
tools.fineprint.label: Check the fine print
tools.fineprint.one: Check the legal surface of the page: policies, consent, trackers, who is behind it.
tools.fineprint.what: Reads the legal surface of the page from what this session already captured: are the privacy, terms, cookie and refund pages there and reachable, was consent asked before anything was stored, does each form ask for consent and only what it needs, who else the page called, and whether there is a real business behind it.
tools.fineprint.why: Nine of the nineteen worries on every "will my site get sued" list are properties of the page, and none of them was checked anywhere in this product. Four more are questions no browser can answer, and those are filed as questions rather than ticked. Accessibility is not re-checked here: "Check accessibility" already does it in more depth.
tools.harvest.label: Map the page
tools.harvest.one: Read every control on the page into a page object a test suite can use.
tools.harvest.what: Reads every button, link and field on the page and gives each one a locator that has been checked against the page, then writes a page map, a Playwright page object and a brief an AI can write tests from.
tools.harvest.why: Writing a page object by hand is an afternoon of guessing selectors. This is that afternoon, done: every locator verified, every guess marked. The three files are in the report under Raw export. Anything you have masked is left out of all three.
tools.inject.label: Try nasty values
tools.inject.one: Point at any field and get the awkward values built for that exact field.
tools.inject.optionsLabel: Which field, and how to clear it
tools.inject.what: Press it and click any field: a text box, a dropdown, a radio, a tickbox, a date, a slider or a rich-text editor. The list offered is built for that field: very long text, Arabic, a date in the year 1800, an emoji, a value the dropdown does not offer, nothing at all.
tools.inject.why: Most bugs live at the edges. This gives you the edges without having to think them up. The field you pick stays picked and outlined until you clear it, so the next value goes where the last one went.
tools.links.label: Check the links
tools.links.one: Ask every link on the page whether it still answers.
tools.links.what: Finds every link on the page and asks each one whether it still answers: broken, redirected, slow, or fine.
tools.links.why: Dead links are the bug every visitor finds and no tester logs. Checked from the extension, so links to other sites are tested too, and the result goes into the session.
tools.mask.label: Mask real data
tools.mask.one: Cover anything on the page so it never reaches a picture, a video or the report.
tools.mask.what: Click any element on the page and a solid block covers the whole of it: a cell, a heading, a photograph, a chart, an embedded frame. Point at a table and every cell is covered separately. It stays covered through every navigation, in every screenshot and in the video, and the words underneath never reach the report or the clipboard.
tools.mask.why: Testing happens on staging systems full of real people. Without this, the first screenshot puts their records into a ticket anyone on the project can open. Click a covered block again to uncover it, or use "Uncover all on this page" on the bar at the top, which leaves the other tabs alone.
tools.perf.label: Check page speed
tools.perf.one: Measure how fast this page really drew and answered, logged in and mid-flow.
tools.perf.what: Measures how fast this page actually drew and responded, plus every request it made.
tools.perf.why: This reads the page as it is right now: logged in, mid-flow, on your real network. That is the number Lighthouse cannot give you.
tools.pick.label: Copy a locator
tools.pick.one: Point at anything and get the one line of code a test needs to find it again.
tools.pick.what: Click any button, field or link on the page and this copies the one line of code a test needs to find it again. Shift+click several, then press Enter, and all of them are copied at once, one per line.
tools.pick.why: Writing that line by hand is slow and easy to get wrong. This checks the line really does match one thing, and only one, before handing it over. Anything you have masked is refused: a locator built out of a covered name would put that name in a test file, which outlives the screenshot the mask was protecting.
tools.record.label: Record the screen
tools.record.one: Film this tab, or the whole screen, into a video kept with the session.
tools.record.what: Films this tab into a video that is kept with the session. Open "Video options" on this row first if you want your microphone, the tab’s sound, or your webcam in it.
tools.record.why: There is no time limit. It runs until you press stop, or the disk fills. Press it again to stop.
tools.rtl.label: Stress the layout
tools.rtl.one: Flip the page right-to-left and lengthen every label, the way a translation would.
tools.rtl.what: Flips the whole page right-to-left and makes every label longer, the way a translation would: 40% longer to start with, and whatever Settings says after you change it.
tools.rtl.why: Shows you which boxes will break when the app is translated, before a translator is ever hired. Anything that cuts text off gets outlined. Press it again to put the page back.
tools.shot.label: Take a screenshot
tools.shot.one: Photograph the page and keep it with the session.
tools.shot.what: Takes a picture of the page and keeps it with the session: either the part on screen, or the whole thing scrolled and stitched into one tall image.
tools.shot.why: A screenshot is the evidence that survives after the page has changed. The whole-page option is for long forms and reports, where the problem is usually below the fold.
tools.spec.label: Reverse-engineer the spec
tools.spec.one: Read this page back as a draft specification, in Arabic and English.
tools.spec.what: Reads this page the way a specification would: every form and what it will accept, every button, where the links go, and the errors it is showing. Writes it up as requirements with acceptance criteria, Arabic and English.
tools.spec.why: Most software this old has no specification, and writing one from scratch is a fortnight. The page already declares half of it: what is required, what pattern a field takes, what the options are. This reads that back, marks what it had to guess, and leaves you editing a draft instead of starting one.
tools.viewport.label: Check another size
tools.viewport.one: Open this same page again in a real window at a phone, tablet or laptop size.
tools.viewport.what: Opens this same page again in a new window at a real phone, tablet or laptop size. The new window carries the session on: it is awake there, and it is masked there if you have masked anything here.
tools.viewport.why: A real window that really reflows, not a zoomed picture of this one. Most layout bugs are found here and need no other browser. What you find in it goes into the report under its own heading, Window sizes, so a phone-sized finding is never filed as though it happened on the desktop.
tools.whitebox.label: Measure code coverage
tools.whitebox.one: Measure which of this page’s own JavaScript actually ran while you used it.
tools.whitebox.optionsLabel: Whether this page can be measured
tools.whitebox.what: Measures which of the page’s own JavaScript actually ran while you used it, function by function.
tools.whitebox.why: Shows the code your test never reached. It uses Chrome’s debugger, so Chrome puts a bar across the top of the window while it runs. That is expected: it comes off the moment you press stop, and nothing is attached until you press start. "Ready?" on this card says in advance whether this page can be measured, and names the reason when it cannot.
